reason: While the text portrays the Hebrews (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל) as a people in conflict with Pharaoh over liberty—specifically their release from slavery in Egypt—the phrase 'on their own land' mischaracterizes the situation. The Israelites are enslaved in Egypt (not on their own land), and the conflict centers on their liberation from captivity and right to leave Egypt to serve God, not on defending or governing their own territory. The passage depicts divine intervention through plagues to compel Pharaoh's compliance, rather than a political or military struggle for territorial sovereignty.
